drip.author: twoferone
drip.title: Started hiding puns in the twins' lunchboxes. They have started writing back
drip.body:
Monday, on the apple slices: "you are both the apple of my eye, equally, don't start." Tuesday, taped to the crackers: "don't crack under pressure."

Today one napkin came home with NO written across it in marker. The other came home with "lettuce eat in peace." There was no lettuce in that lunch. He brought the pun in from outside. I have never been so proud or so outnumbered.

comments.author: beavertales
comments.body: bringing outside lettuce into a pun fight is advanced play. that kid isn't writing back, he's negotiating

replies.author: twoferone
replies.body: tomorrow's is already taped to a banana. it says "I'd never split you two up." there will be a response and I'm scared of it

comments.author: ISO_a_good_time
comments.body: the NO in marker is the harshest review I've ever seen and it still technically counts as a note

comments.author: brasstacks_barb
comments.body: Retired teacher. A lot of lunchbox notes crossed my desk over the years, and the ones that talked back were always my favourites. The lettuce one is going to be a wonderful problem for some lucky teacher.

replies.author: twoferone
replies.body: he's already asking which other vegetables have jokes in them. I've made something I can't control

comments.author: OttomanEmpire
comments.body: keep going. the day one of them tapes a pun to your coffee mug, you'll know the torch has been passed

drip.author: beavertales
drip.title: Apple season fact: every McIntosh you've ever eaten traces back to one tree on a farm about an hour from Ottawa
drip.body:
Apples don't grow true from seed, so every McIntosh orchard anywhere was grafted from cuttings going back to that one tree found in eastern Ontario.

Which makes it the only family tree where everyone at the reunion is the same person. Bought a bag to celebrate. They all agreed with me.

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: a whole family where everyone's the same? I've got two from the same batch and they can't agree on which cereal is the good one. these apples have discipline

replies.author: beavertales
replies.body: the orchard is quieter too. no apple has ever asked for the bigger half

comments.author: seed_vault
comments.body: Heritage gardener here: it's also why planting a McIntosh seed gets you a completely different apple, usually a small sour one. Nature's way of telling you not to get clever.

replies.author: beavertales
replies.body: so the seed is the one that falls far from the tree. every family has one

comments.author: OttomanEmpire
comments.body: for the record the Empire apple is a cross between a McIntosh and a Red Delicious. so I'm related to this tree now, and it's the first empire in my family that's still standing

comments.author: ISO_a_good_time
comments.body: so every McIntosh is basically a stock photo. one original, licensed everywhere

drip.author: ISO_a_good_time
drip.title: Someone asked why I always shoot in RAW
drip.body:
I like my photos the way I like my feelings. Unprocessed.

Mentioned this to my therapist as a joke. She did not take it as a joke. We have a lot to work on.

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: at some point you have to export those feelings. even as a low-quality JPEG. just get them out of the folder

replies.author: ISO_a_good_time
replies.body: can't. the folder is mostly blurry duplicates of the same feeling

comments.author: beavertales
comments.body: she's not going to let you white balance your way out of this one

comments.author: OttomanEmpire
comments.body: I go the other way. take whatever's going on and staple a nice fabric over it so nobody sees the frame

replies.author: ISO_a_good_time
replies.body: very comfortable coping mechanism. terrible for your posture

comments.author: FocalPointFran
comments.body: Wedding photographer. The RAW files are where the truth lives. The JPEGs are the version we show the in-laws.

drip.author: twoferone
drip.title: Took the twins through a corn maze today and warned them not to share any secrets in there
drip.body:
Too many ears.

One of them whispered "that's corny" and his brother shushed him. They believe me now. I don't know how to walk this back.

comments.author: ISO_a_good_time
comments.body: hope nobody got stalked

replies.author: twoferone
replies.body: a teenager in a scarecrow costume followed us for three rows. it was his job but it felt personal

comments.author: beavertales
comments.body: aw shucks. I was going to call this a-maize-ing but I promised my wife I'd retire that one

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: Took my goalie to one of these last fall and he found the exit in four minutes by walking straight through the corn. No respect for the institution.

replies.author: twoferone
replies.body: that's not cheating, that's thinking outside the rows

comments.author: OttomanEmpire
comments.body: since we're a safe distance from the corn, a confession: I once got lost in a hay bale maze. waist height. built for toddlers

drip.author: beavertales
drip.title: Day and night are the same length today
drip.body:
Which makes tonight an even-ing.

Said it at supper. My wife got up and moved to the other end of the table, so now the seating isn't even either. Can't win, even on the one day that's supposed to be fair.

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: the one day the whole planet is split down the middle and she picks a side. respect

comments.author: constellation_prize
comments.body: Hate to be the astronomy person, but the equinox isn't a whole day. It happens at one exact moment, which this time is just after eight in the evening, Eastern.

replies.author: beavertales
replies.body: so the even-ing is literally in the evening. I've never been this right by accident

replies.author: OttomanEmpire
replies.body: one exact moment on the calendar and he still landed a pun on it. most precise thing ever done in this room

comments.author: ISO_a_good_time
comments.body: a joke timed to the actual orbit of the earth. the dedication is astronomical. the joke is fine

drip.author: OttomanEmpire
drip.title: Client asked if my prices went up because of inflation
drip.body:
Told her no, I don't do air mattresses.

She paid the quote. I think mostly so she could leave.

comments.author: beavertales
comments.body: that really let the air out of the conversation

replies.author: OttomanEmpire
replies.body: I've been told my bedside manner is deflating. I've also been told to stop saying bedside manner to people dropping off footstools

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: the twins asked me what inflation was last week. I blew up a balloon and let it go across the kitchen. they now believe the economy is loud and ends up behind the fridge

comments.author: IndexFundIrene
comments.body: Boring-money person here. I've tried to explain inflation at more dinners than I'd like to admit, and the balloon behind the fridge is the first version I'd actually steal.

comments.author: ISO_a_good_time
comments.body: you should knock a bit off memory foam though. it remembers what it used to cost

replies.author: OttomanEmpire
replies.body: memory foam never forgets a price. that's why it sighs when you sit on it

drip.author: ISO_a_good_time
drip.title: My therapist asked if this moon photography thing is just a phase
drip.body:
Told her there are eight of them, so realistically this is going to take a while.

For the record, last night's full moon came out great. Two hundred shots, three of them sharp. That's growth.

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: eight phases is a big commitment. I've been in my dad joke phase since the twins were born and there's no waning in sight

replies.author: ISO_a_good_time
replies.body: can't wait for your new moon phase. nobody will be able to see the jokes at all

comments.author: OttomanEmpire
comments.body: she's right to be concerned. sounds like you've been moonlighting

comments.author: orbital_decay
comments.body: The moon is always a full sphere with one half lit. The phases are just how much of that lit half we can see from here. So technically it's one moon at different angles of commitment.

replies.author: ISO_a_good_time
replies.body: different angles of commitment is almost word for word what my therapist said about me

comments.author: beavertales
comments.body: rained out here last night, so I'll take your word for it. sounds like the moon's been working on itself too

drip.author: OttomanEmpire
drip.title: Couple dropped off their couch. She called it a couch, he called it a chesterfield, and they asked me to settle it
drip.body:
So I told them it's a settee.

Neither of them was happy, which is how you know it was a fair ruling.

comments.author: beavertales
comments.body: chesterfield gang. we're a dying breed but we're very comfortable

replies.author: OttomanEmpire
replies.body: the chesterfield people are always the ones who still have the plastic covers on. you're preserving more than a word

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: the twins call ours the trampoline, and at this point the springs agree with them

comments.author: sump_pump_sam
comments.body: My house came with a chesterfield the previous owners left in the basement. It's been down there longer than the furnace. I don't think it can legally leave anymore.

replies.author: OttomanEmpire
replies.body: a basement chesterfield that old isn't furniture anymore, it's a tenant

comments.author: ISO_a_good_time
comments.body: the correct answer is chesterfield at your grandparents' place and couch everywhere else. every canadian is bilingual in furniture

late_comments.author: beavertales
late_comments.body: came back to this now that school's back in. does this year's teacher know what's coming, or is somebody going to warn them

late_comments.author: twoferone
late_comments.body: reread this with my first pumpkin spice of the season in hand. your buddy got out right before the busiest stretch of the year. that's not quitting, that's timing

late_comments.author: ISO_a_good_time
late_comments.body: found this again after trying to redo the padding on my camera strap. can confirm upholstery is just photography where the mistakes get stapled in
